cards.text: During David's reign, a famine hits for three years in a row. Not one bad year, not two, THREE, and that's not a rough patch anymore, friend, that's a lifestyle. So David seeks the face of the LORD.

cards.question: David asks the LORD about the three-year famine. What does the LORD say it's because of?

answers.text: Blood Saul shed killing the Gibeonites
Idols the people set up in the land

cards.text: So David calls in the Gibeonites. Quick background, friend: they're not Israelites. They're what's left of the Amorites.

cards.question: The Israelites had taken an oath concerning the Gibeonites, and Saul kept it.

cards.text: In his zeal for Israel and Judah, Saul sought to kill them. Now it's on David's desk, like starting a new job and finding the last guy's overdue invoice waiting in your inbox.

cards.question: David asks the Gibeonites how he can make amends. What does he hope they'll do after?

answers.text: Bless the inheritance of the LORD

cards.question: The Gibeonites ask David to pay them silver and gold from Saul's house.

cards.text: They also tell David he shouldn't put anyone in Israel to death for them. 'Whatever you ask, I will do for you,' he replies, and friend, those are BIG words to say before you've heard the ask.

cards.question: The Gibeonites talk about the man who consumed them and plotted to wipe them out of Israel. What do they ask David to hand over?

answers.text: Half of the land Saul held

cards.text: There it is, friend, THE ask: the Gibeonites want to hang the seven before the LORD at Gibeah of Saul. I bet you could hear a chocolate chip drop.

cards.question: David turns down the Gibeonites' request for seven of Saul's descendants.

cards.text: But one of Saul's grandsons is spared: Mephibosheth, the son of Saul's son Jonathan.

cards.question: Why does David spare Mephibosheth son of Jonathan?

answers.text: Because of his oath with Jonathan
Because the Gibeonites left him out
Because Mephibosheth was still a child

cards.text: Careful now, friend, because there's ANOTHER Mephibosheth, a son of Saul himself. Two Mephibosheths in one story, like two guys named Mike on the same work team.

cards.question: David takes this other Mephibosheth and his brother Armoni. Who was their mother?

cards.text: Then David takes the sons of Saul's daughter Merab, the sons she bore to Adriel son of Barzillai the Meholathite. That's a LOT of name, friend, and here I am with just 'Dorin' carved on a handle, grateful for every letter.

cards.question: Two sons from Rizpah plus ___ sons from Merab make the seven the Gibeonites asked for.

cards.text: This one's heavy, friend: David hands all seven over to the Gibeonites, and they hang them on the hill before the LORD. All seven fall together.

cards.question: The seven are put to death at the beginning of the ___ harvest.

cards.text: Now watch Rizpah, the mother of Armoni and Mephibosheth. She takes sackcloth and spreads it out for herself on a rock.

cards.question: Day and night on that rock, what does Rizpah keep away from the bodies?

answers.text: Birds by day and beasts by night
Thieves by day and soldiers by night
Strangers by day and robbers by night

cards.question: Rizpah keeps watch over the bodies from the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven pours down on them.

cards.text: Word of what Rizpah has done reaches David. Then David gets moving: he goes and takes the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the men of Jabesh-gilead.
Here's the backstory, friend: those men had stolen the bones from a public square, where the Philistines had hung the bodies after striking Saul down at Gilboa.

cards.question: The Philistines had hung the bodies of Saul and Jonathan in the public square of ___.
David brings back the bones of Saul and Jonathan but leaves the bones of the seven who were hanged where they are.

cards.text: They bury the bones of Saul and Jonathan in Zela, in the land of Benjamin. I spent years in the back of a drawer, friend, so I know what it means when somebody finally comes back for you.

cards.question: In Zela, whose tomb are Saul and Jonathan buried in?
They do everything King David commanded. What happens after that?

answers.text: God answers their prayers for the land
The Gibeonites move away from Israel
Saul's family turns against King David

findings.problem: Saul first appears in this card's answer, and later on stop 1 cards 3 and 5, but no card ever says who he is (Israel's king before David). The baker has to bring that in from outside the lesson.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Rizpah is never mentioned before this card. Stop 2 card 3 only says there is another Mephibosheth. All three answers are names the baker hasn't seen, so the right pick comes down to luck. Rizpah is only introduced afterward, on stop 2 card 9.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The blank asks for 'barley', a word from the text the baker hasn't seen. Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason barley over wheat or grape.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the place name 'Beth-shan'. Stop 2 card 13 only says 'a public square', so the baker is guessing wording they haven't seen, with no meaning to reason from.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Merab's sons are being taken to be hanged. On that same card, Papa Dorin jokes about how long their father's name is. Joking at this moment doesn't treat their situation with respect, and it doesn't fit the moment.

rule.text: Humor about people in Bible stories looks at their human situation with respect.

findings.problem: About half the choice cards can't be reasoned out from earlier cards. These are stop 1 cards 2, 6, 7 and 9, and stop 2 cards 2, 4, 8 and 14. That's 8 of 16. For example, stop 1 card 6 ('bless the inheritance of the LORD') and stop 1 card 7 (silver and gold) have no setup before them. That is more than 'a few' discovery questions.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
